summary: A husband and wife argue about politics daily, talk over each other and stay tied to a short list of shared stands.
realLife: A married couple on opposite sides said they fight about politics more than anything and clash at least once a day. She asks pointed questions about whether his party is consistent; he answers with sarcasm and lines that wave her off. Nothing is off limits, they talk over each other, and neither has moved the other. They share two stands, one on abortion rights and one on unions, and she says disagreeing does not mean she loves him less.
sources: https://www.nprillinois.org/post/hes-trump-shes-biden-how-married-couple-navigate-political-differences (NPR piece on a politically divided married couple in Colorado)
gates: at least two stands they share on the record
weights: how combative both are by trait
how often they are home together
inGame: reads the tie between speaker and listener and each side's stand with its reason; the shared stands are where the two stand records agree
